title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained both joined complaints, annulled Arizona Presbytery’s deposition of TE John Evans, and remanded the matter for further action consistent with the decision.
first_summary: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded because BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts. Evans could not approve facts presented after he left the meeting. Presbytery remained free to address the underlying matter in further proceedings.
summary: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it.

sources.supports: Joined-case identity, complaint, judgment, adopted reasoning, relief, and approval by the full SJC.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Cases 2019-10 and 2019-12 were joined; the full SJC sustained the complaints and approved the decision, 18-3-0. Lines 13–25, 216–218; printed pp. 771–779.
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaints challenged Presbytery’s April 26, 2019 use of BCO 38-1 to depose Evans without process. Lines 23–25, 141–147; printed pp. 772, 776.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC found Evans had not approved the additional facts presented by the investigative committee, sustained the complaints, annulled the judgment, and remanded. Lines 171–214; printed pp. 777–779.
evidence_notes.qualifications: No meeting or detailed discussion was expressly required; the underlying matter was unaffected and could proceed with process, without process, or be dismissed. The later concurrence and amendment proposals were not adopted reasoning. Lines 184–193, 205–214, 220–258; printed pp. 777–781.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No external decision was incorporated by reference as the basis of the judgment.

source_limits: The supplied source contains the adopted decision and a separate concurrence, but not the complete consolidated record or party briefs.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the deposition without process and the unapproved investigative material.
score_reasons.decision: States that both complaints were sustained, the deposition annulled, and the matter remanded.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the failure to obtain Evans’s approval of the full factual basis.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves both the approved-statement requirement and the rejection of a mandatory meeting requirement.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted ruling from the concurrence and leaves the underlying merits unresolved.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the procedural defect, remedy, and remaining options.

verification_notes: Rechecked the judgment at lines 145–147 and reasoning at lines 184–214. The final summary adds the rejected claim that BCO 38-1 requires a meeting or detailed discussion and clarifies that the underlying matter remained open to several dispositions.
